question.problem: What is the length of the hypotenuse in a $30^\circ$-$60^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangle if the side opposite the $30^\circ$ angle has a length of $6\,\textrm{cm}?$
question.worked_solution:
Let's refer to our standard $30^\circ$-$60^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangle.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14165760/assets/5fe1cd7975f1537bead1f9560816dafe5e8f3ec0db3e683e2bd3e00c4ac54506.png)

In any $30^\circ$-$60^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangle, the hypotenuse is twice the length of the shorter leg.

The leg opposite the $30^\circ$ angle is the shorter leg of the triangle. So here, the shorter leg has length $x=6\, \text{cm}.$

So here, the length of the hypotenuse must be

$$
2 \cdot 6 = 12\,\textrm{cm}.
$$
